title: Fourier formula for flip disagreement
statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$, and let $S\subseteq[n]$. If $x^S$ is obtained by flipping the coordinates in $S$, then
\[
\frac14\E_x[(f(x)-f(x^S))^2]
=\frac{1-\displaystyle\sum_{T\subseteq[n]}(-1)^{|T\cap S|}\widehat f(T)^2}{2},
\]
where $\widehat f(T)=\E_x[f(x)\chi_T(x)]$ and $\chi_T(x)=\prod_{i\in T}\sigma(x_i)$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. For $S\subseteq[n]$, let $x^S$ be the bit vector obtained by flipping exactly the coordinates in $S$. If $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, then $\Pr[f(x)\ne f(x^S)]=(1-\sum_{T\subseteq[n]}(-1)^{|T\cap S|}\widehat f(T)^2)/2$ for each $S\subseteq[n]$; equivalently, this is $\tfrac14\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^S))^2]$.
